gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: Look at Sam — he ___ at that stranger again.
gaps.hint: look draws attention to this moment
gaps.explanation: 'Look' draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used: is staring.

gaps.sentence: Jane ___ her phone at home, and it drives me mad.
gaps.hint: annoying habit shown with always continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Always' with the present continuous expresses an irritating habit: is always leaving.

gaps.sentence: As soon as the plane landed, everyone ___ their phones.
gaps.hint: as soon as links two past actions
gaps.explanation: 'As soon as' links two sequential completed actions, so the past simple is used: switched on.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: When you ___ John tomorrow, please give him my regards.
gaps.hint: no will after when for the future
gaps.explanation: In time clauses referring to the future, English uses the present simple, not 'will': see.
